# the contributor audit: five-fiber augmentation, cone laws, and the mixed Hessian

All three results below are valid in their stated scope. None supplies the missing general OC inequality.

## Five interval fibers

Source: `candidate dcd790485c83acdc`.

The cap knot tables are exhaustive: a through-mark line changes a fiber's clipping status only at either endpoint slope. Distinctness and the strict gaps in the displayed tables justify the full local chamber, including the plateau endpoints. Thus the exact local expression Q=max((w0+w1+w2)/2,w2/2+w3+w4) is valid for arbitrary sufficiently small compatible endpoint perturbations, not just centered fibers. The upper certificate covers every candidate line. Pure base cuts retain a strict gap for the lower certificate.

Discrete concavity gives M<=5w2 and hence 3Q>=M+w2/2>=11M/10. Equality forces affine widths; equality in the endpoint convexity/concavity constraints then forces affine centers. This really obstructs fixed-support monotone elimination, within continuous sampled-endpoint topology. It does not assert a local minimum for arbitrary Hausdorff perturbations of the ambient body.

The preserving point extension is valid. Its left point is on the old upper affine roof and above the old lower affine extension. Its right point lies between both affine extensions. The original fibers therefore remain exactly fixed under convex hull and the nested Minkowski path. New integer fibers first appear as points, so contribute no H1 mass and have depth zero.

For the growing fibers K_-1=[15/2-u,15/2], K5=[-u/4,u/4], 0<u<3, all four endpoint slope inequalities have the correct directions. The two left-group caps through (1,u/6) have masses 33/2+u/2. Their margin sum is -4(z-1); the right-group margins sum to 20(z-2). Hence every point of every integer plane is covered by these actual four caps. This includes all newly created candidate points without a perturbative gap argument. Total mass is 45+3u/2, and the derivative of the common upper depth bound is -9/[4(45+3u/2)^2]. The certificate proves strict improvement from u=0; it does not, by itself, prove that the actual optimized depth is monotone between every pair u>0.

## Arbitrary centered slope laws on one affine cone

Source: `candidate 6146c77d1d7c5e08`.

Substitution x=r(z)v identifies each slope with a uniform base layer. The ray threshold is t=H/(B-b); b>1 contributes a whole ray, whereas b<1 contributes a truncated ray. This verifies P/V=p0 e+1-v, C/C0=e and the stated M formula, including the full-ray term.

The fixed upper truncation endpoint b=1 has no atom under any mixture of finite uniform layers and an atom at zero. On compact parameter subintervals, the first two energy derivatives are uniformly bounded on the negative tail. Therefore M=0 really implies that e attains its minimum at the actual projective parameter.

The layer bound has I_k''(x)=-k/(x+k)^3. Jensen applies to the probability law of layers, including radius zero and unbounded finite radii. The exponent comparison has the correct direction for both positive and negative b: log(1+t)>=t/(1+t) holds throughout t>-1. Thus 2v-1<=e<=(2v-1)/v is justified, with the v=1 case separate.

The common correction yields (P-cC)/V=1-v+4e/9. Its lower bound is (5-v)/9>=4/9. Its upper gap is (3v-2)^2/(9v)>=0. Both inequalities therefore hold for every separately centered law with the SAME c. Weighted cancellation gives the claimed two-law bound, whenever its denominator is positive. A compactification atom at infinity has P/V=1/2 and C=M=0, so the extension is valid. No cone replacement of a general profile follows from this audit.

## Fixed-normal mixed-volume Hessian

Source: `candidate d0bf1dbafd292ae0`.

The actual common ambient inequalities give fibers ell_h(z)K. At each integer k, the unique lowest roof remains k because its gap against roof j is epsilon(j-k)^2+h_j-h_k>epsilon/2. Positivity and boundedness hold on the full real base interval. Thus every sampled radius is independently variable in the asserted parameter cube, despite a fixed common list of ambient normals.

The exact mixed mass is |K| sum r_k^d. Its Hessian is diagonal positive definite of arbitrary rank for d>=2. A blanket Alexandrov--Fenchel signature statement for mixed volume is therefore false, already for one integer coordinate. Differentiating r^d F(c/r) twice gives precisely the displayed cap Hessian. The normalized cap difference can cancel the mass Hessian, so the stopping test does not refute a theorem that uses all actual stationarity and source-tie constraints.
